CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for reassessment of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing that he has experienced a slight improvement in his overall anxiety levels, but continues to struggle with sleep disturbances and fatigue. He reports that while the sertraline dosage of 100 mg daily remains effective in managing his anxiety during the day, he still averages only 5 hours of sleep per night, frequently waking up throughout the night. The cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) has been beneficial, yet he finds it challenging to maintain consistent sleep hygiene practices due to work-related stress.
Mr. Smith notes that his tension-type headaches have persisted, occurring 4 to 5 times a week, with moderate intensity. He has been using ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, which provides temporary relief, but he seeks alternative strategies to reduce the frequency and intensity of these headaches. Additionally, he describes persistent fatigue that he attributes to both inadequate sleep and the ongoing stressors of his job.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 100 mg daily 2. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith reports he continues to work as a software engineer and has maintained his walking routine three times a week. He has made efforts to incorporate brief stretching exercises during work hours to alleviate tension. He continues to consume alcohol socially and has not resumed tobacco use. He expresses a strong interest in exploring additional stress management techniques and has been attending weekly mindfulness meditation sessions, which he finds helpful.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Reports ongoing anxiety, persistent sleep disturbances, no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms noted. - Neurological: Tension-type headaches as described, no visual changes or focal neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. - General: Persistent fatigue, no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, no motor or sensory deficits. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative, maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with ongoing anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline 100 mg daily; consider referral to a psychiatrist for evaluation of potential augmentation therapy with an atypical antipsychotic or benzodiazepine if no significant improvement is noted by the next visit. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin 3 mg at bedtime; reinforce CBT-I strategies and sleep hygiene practices, and consider a sleep study if symptoms persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen 400 mg as needed; initiate a trial of amitriptyline 10 mg nightly for headache prophylaxis and monitor for efficacy and tolerability. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage ongoing physical activity and mindfulness practices; discuss the incorporation of relaxation techniques such as guided imagery or progressive muscle relaxation.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-01-01 to evaluate symptoms and treatment effectiveness. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or side effects from medications.
